score_meanings.promise_vocabulary: 0 drifts into claims/profiles/central trust-ledger framing, 5 stays promise-first and pCID-specific
score_meanings.simplicity_durability: 0 overbuilt or fragile, 5 minimal, durable, and small-device-friendly under the 100-year goal

promise_theory_rules: A promise is a scoped declaration of intent.
No agent can make a promise on behalf of another agent.
Trust is a local assessment of whether a promise will be kept.
Promises to receive or use are not equivalent to obligations, impositions, or promises to give.
promise_theory_references: Mark Burgess, In Search of Certainty
Mark Burgess, Promise Theory: Principles and Applications

assessment.rationale: A small deterministic three-slot envelope fits PromiseGrid’s durability and local-evidence goals well, and its unknown-pCID policy is compatible with peer-local assessment. But this scenario asks whether local observations can drive pull/keep/advertise decisions without tokens, and the specimen is only an envelope layer, not a full local-assessment protocol. It helps carry signed evidence, yet it does not itself model storage outcomes, peer accounting, or explicit promise language.
strengths: Very small explicit artifact: deterministic CBOR array [pcid, payload, signature].
Signs canonical [pcid, payload], binding payload bytes to protocol identity.
Unknown-pCID policy supports blind carry without false verification claims.
Avoids central registry or token requirement at the envelope layer.
weaknesses: Weak direct fit to the scenario because it does not define local assessment records or decision logic.
Promise-Theory vocabulary is limited; the draft is protocol-centric rather than promise-first.
Generic peers may struggle to compare proofs across protocols because proof rules are delegated to pcid-specific handlers.
risks: Proof semantics hidden behind payload pCID may reduce audit clarity for generic peers.
Changing proof families may require minting new payload pCIDs, creating evolution friction.
The envelope can transport evidence of behavior but does not by itself express the promises and observations needed for local economic decisions.
open_questions: Can a generic peer make useful local trust assessments when proof-family details are hidden behind the payload pCID?
Does coupling proof evolution to payload pCID force avoidable pCID churn over time?
What payload-level promises would explicitly connect signed envelopes to observations such as kept storage promises or corrupt chunks?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.

autonomous_agents.note: Peers choose locally whether to preserve, parse, verify, trust, or ignore an envelope.

scoped_intent.note: Mostly framed as protocol mechanics and verification rules rather than explicit agent-scoped promises, so it needs PT-oriented reframing.

no_promises_for_others.note: The envelope does not let one agent promise on behalf of another.

no_guaranteed_outcomes.note: Signatures verify bytes, not outcomes; the draft does not claim guarantees about behavior or storage success.

local_trust_assessment.note: Unknown-pCID handling preserves local evidence without claiming global verification; trust remains peer-local.

accept_use_not_obligation.note: The design carries signed evidence and does not redefine receipt or use as obligation.

violations: The draft is not promise-first; it specifies wire-format and proof semantics more than agent-scoped declarations of intent.
